headline: Meteorologists Baffled By Cedar Street's Persistent 'Slightly Different' Weather
summary: Two-block stretch experiences temperatures exactly 3 degrees cooler than surrounding areas, wind from 'unusual direction.'
content:
Residents of the 200 block of Cedar Street have long suspected what local meteorologists confirmed this week: their neighborhood exists in what scientists are calling a "highly localized microclimate" that defies easy explanation.

"It's always just a little bit off," said longtime resident Patricia Okonkwo, 67, who has lived on Cedar Street for 31 years. "My sister lives two blocks over and she'll call saying it's gorgeous outside. I look out my window and there's this... mist. Not fog, not rain. Just mist. Hovering."

Weather station data collected over the past 18 months shows that the 200 block of Cedar Street consistently registers temperatures 2.7 to 3.4 degrees Fahrenheit cooler than the surrounding area. Wind readings indicate breezes that "don't correspond to any regional pattern," according to Dr. Helen Marsh of the Municipal Weather Service.

"The wind on Cedar Street appears to come from a direction we can only describe as 'diagonal-ish,'" Dr. Marsh noted in her preliminary report. "This shouldn't be meteorologically significant, but we've had to invent a new notation for it."

Some residents have embraced the phenomenon. Local gardener Tom Bliss claims the unique conditions are "perfect for heirloom tomatoes" and has won the county fair three years running.

Others remain frustrated. "I've had to buy a separate wardrobe just for walking to my car," said resident Marcus Webb. "Three degrees doesn't sound like much until you're the only person on the bus in a sweater in July."

The weather service plans to install additional monitoring equipment pending budget approval. In the meantime, they recommend Cedar Street residents "dress in layers and remain philosophical."
author: Daniel Frost, Weather Desk
